doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: The KMOX four-hour jazz radio show
summary: Wolff describes his Saturday-night show on KMOX, his freedom over programming, and using it as a teaching tool.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Can you tell me a little more about your radio work?

Yeah. I’m real thrilled with the show I’m doing right now which is a four hour jazz show on KMOX which is a 50,000 clear channel watt station, it reaches some 48 states. I get phone calls from all over the country and Canada every Saturday night. It’s a very powerful midwestern station which also is the sports voice of St. Louis so we have the Cardinals which reach a great many homes, and I come on after the ball game. We have

the blues and so it’s a sports station and it’s a talk radio station, and one of the few AM stations that’s really survived in a marketplace that they’ve become relics. But this particular station is quite successful and they allow me to bring in my own music, I’ve never been told that I can’t play this or I can’t play that, so I have total freedom and independence in what I do and so I design my programs as if I’m the listener. And I figure that if I’m going to enjoy the music, chances are my listeners will too. But I’ve got to enjoy it first or I don’t put it on. So when I get calls for Lawrence Welk, he doesn’t make my show.
I guess you can only go by your own tastes and your own likes, you know you can’t second guess your audience.

Well I view the audience as really one who is interested in the music for a number of reasons, not the least of which I hope is to learn a little bit more about the music. So I use the four hour show as really a teaching tool. And I really think that’s what gives me the most pleasure, the fact that I enjoy the music that goes along with it makes it even that much more fun. But I’m getting an opportunity not only to share music I love, but to teach other people how to appreciate it. That’s a good feeling.
